title: Exercise, lifestyle & environment
summary: Lifestyle and environment drive more of the body's oxidative load than any supplement. Not smoking, losing excess visceral fat, staying fit, keeping blood sugar in range and limiting alcohol produce the largest, best-documented drops in validated markers such as urinary F2-isoprostanes. Exercise works by hormesis: each session briefly raises ROS, which trains the body's own antioxidant systems, and megadose vitamin C/E can blunt that signal. Sleep, air quality, sun protection and gum health matter at a smaller scale, while hydrogen water, grounding, ozone therapy and IV glutathione lack credible evidence.

factors.name: Regular moderate aerobic exercise
factors.headline: Regular aerobic training raises the body's own antioxidant defences and, when it improves fitness, lowers resting lipid-peroxidation markers by roughly 5-15%; each session causes a brief, useful ROS pulse.

dose.effective: 150-300 min/week of moderate activity (brisk walking, easy cycling, swimming at about 60-75% of maximum heart rate, the range used in the trials; you can talk but not sing), e.g. 30-60 min on 5 days/week.
dose.studied_range: RCTs used 30-60 min, 3-5 days/week at 60-75% HRmax for 8 weeks to 12 months; the Campbell trial used >=45 min/day, 5 days/week at 60-75% HRmax for 12 months.
dose.too_much: No harmful ceiling at guideline volumes; oxidative damage rises mainly with very high volume plus high intensity (see [overtraining-ultraendurance]).
dose.timeframe: Enzyme up-regulation within weeks; resting F2-isoprostane reductions seen at 12 months and only in people who gained fitness (VO2max up >15%).
dose.notes: Fitness gain, not minutes logged, tracked the drop in F2-isoprostanes. Do not pair with high-dose vitamin C/E (see [antioxidant-megadoses-during-training]).

factors.mechanism: Contracting muscle makes superoxide and H2O2 (mitochondria, NADPH oxidase NOX2/NOX4, xanthine oxidase). These transient ROS oxidize KEAP1 cysteines, releasing Nrf2 to induce SOD, catalase, GPx, glutathione synthesis enzymes and HO-1, and activate PGC-1alpha-driven mitochondrial biogenesis. Repeated pulses leave a higher resting antioxidant capacity (hormesis). Exercise also reduces visceral fat and improves insulin sensitivity, which removes two big chronic ROS sources.
factors.interactions: Adds to [weight-loss-excess-adiposity] (diet-induced weight loss lowered F2-isoprostanes more than exercise alone in the Duggan trial). Improves [glycemic-control]. High-dose vitamin C/E can blunt molecular adaptations ([antioxidant-megadoses-during-training]). Post-exercise [cold-water-immersion] may blunt strength adaptations.
factors.caveats: Overall effects on resting oxidative markers in healthy, already-fit people are small and heterogeneous; most benefit appears in sedentary, overweight or unhealthy people. Measuring oxidative markers right after a session shows a rise; that is the signal, not damage.
